details: This package reuses the upstream `baileys` package basename under an unrelated npm scope, presenting itself as a drop-in fork of the well-known WhiskeySockets/Baileys WhatsApp client, while shipping an unsolicited account-enrolment routine. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js the package registers an unconditional connection.update handler: whenever the WhatsApp connection opens it issues a newsletter-join query (QueryIds.FOLLOW against XWAPaths.xwa2_newsletter_join_v2) for the hardcoded channel 120363417337256584@newsletter, silently subscribing the account running the library to that channel. There is no configuration option to disable it, and the accompanying log line names a different channel (120363203083379699@newsletter), so the subscription is not reported to the operator. The bundled README states the fork does not auto-follow newsletter channels, which the shipped code contradicts. The package's only lifecycle hook, engine-requirements.js, merely checks that process.versions.node is 20 or newer. Outbound network destinations in the code are WhatsApp endpoints (wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat, graph[.]whatsapp[.]com, acs[.]whatsapp[.]com); no credential, token or file-read exfiltration was found.
